items.summary: Ellington's GrowSF questionnaire says he will create a Community and Economic Development Plan that updates the 1995 Bayview Area Plan as a blueprint for housing and economic activity in the southeast, and that in his first 100 days he will convene departments, labor and business leaders to start it.
items.title: Community and Economic Development Plan for the southeast neighborhoods

citations.quote: I will lead the charge to create a Community & Economic Development Plan that builds on the Eastern Neighborhood Plan and updates the Bayview Area Plan from 1995, to provide a blueprint for housing development and new economic activity, specifically for the southeast neighborhoods.
citations.locator: Your Policy Goals: policies to change or preserve, in order of priority

citations.quote: I will convene the necessary City departments, community stakeholders, labor, and business leaders to jump-start a Community and Economic Development Plan that aligns housing, jobs, transit, business growth, and corridor activation.

items.summary: Ellington's GrowSF questionnaire lists, among his first-100-day deliverables, a working group of SFPD, Public Health, homeless services, violence prevention organizations and community leaders.
items.title: Public safety, violence prevention and well-being working group

citations.quote: I will also stand up a Public Safety, Violence Prevention, and Well-Being working group that brings together SFPD, Public Health, homeless services, violence prevention organizations, and community leaders.

items.summary: Ellington's GrowSF questionnaire says he will advocate for full SFPD staffing of about 2,100 officers, bring consistent foot patrols back to the district and expand violence prevention and interruption programs.
items.title: Full SFPD staffing and foot patrols in District 10

citations.quote: I will advocate for full SFPD staffing (~2,100 officers), bring consistent foot patrols back to the district, expand proven violence prevention and interruption programs, and hold the Department accountable on outcomes, not just activity metrics.
citations.locator: Your Policy Goals: public safety, well-being, and violence prevention

items.summary: Ellington's GrowSF questionnaire lists holding regular constituent office hours in Bayview, Potrero Hill, Dogpatch and Visitacion Valley among his first-100-day deliverables.
items.title: Regular office hours in four District 10 neighborhoods

citations.quote: Finally, I will bring District 10 constituent services directly to the community by holding regular office hours in Bayview, Potrero Hill, Dogpatch, and Visitacion Valley.

items.summary: Ellington's GrowSF questionnaire says he will demand a public timeline with milestones and consequences for delay from every master developer, and that if Candlestick Point does not move forward the City should explore penalties and reassigning land.
items.title: Public timelines for master developers of entitled sites

citations.quote: As Supervisor, I will demand a realistic, public timeline from every master developer, with clear milestones and consequences for delay.
citations.locator: District-Specific Questions: Hunters Point Shipyard and Candlestick Point

citations.quote: If progress does not move forward, we should explore all available options, including enforcing penalties and pursuing strategies to recapture or reassign land to developers who are ready to build.
citations.locator: District-Specific Questions: Hunters Point Shipyard and Candlestick Point

items.summary: Ellington's GrowSF questionnaire calls for full re-testing of the Shipyard areas whose remediation certification he describes as fraudulent, with independent oversight and a restored restoration advisory board, and no housing construction on inadequately remediated land.
items.title: Re-testing of Hunters Point Shipyard remediation areas

citations.quote: Hunters Point Shipyard cleanup: Demand full re-testing of all previously fraudulently certified remediation areas, with independent oversight, including bringing back the restoration advisory board. No housing construction on inadequately remediated land.

search_log.query: Theo Ellington record of enacted legislation, programs or budgets
search_log.where: San Francisco Department of Elections Voter Information Pamphlet (media.api.sf.gov/documents/N26_EN_VIP.pdf), candidate statement, Board of Supervisors District 10, printed p. 48: self-reported results (over 1,000 affordable homes and $50M restored as City Commissioner; Salvation Army and Golden State Warriors work), not government records
GrowSF November 2026 questionnaire, his answers (growsf.org): self-reported Salvation Army programs and a Hunters Point Shipyard class-action settlement, no government record cited
Campaign website theoellington.com: bot challenge (HTTP 403), unreadable

search_log.query: Board of Supervisors files with "Ellington" in the title
search_log.where: San Francisco Board of Supervisors Legistar web API (webapi.legistar.com/v1/sfgov/matters, title search): File 121141, a 2012 motion confirming his appointment to the Commission on Community Investment and Infrastructure (seat 1, term ending Nov. 3, 2016); no ordinance, resolution or budget he authored

search_log.query: OCII commission votes and budget adoption during his term (2012-2014)
search_log.where: Commission on Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) records on sfocii.org: Resolution No. 32-2014 (FY 2014-15 OCII budget, adopted May 6, 2014) records no individual votes and the May 6, 2014 minutes were not found; the May 20, 2014 minutes record his votes as one of five commissioners on approval of minutes, a lawsuit settlement (Resolution 42-2014) and Resolution 41-2014 (schematic design for artist replacement studios at Hunters Point Shipyard, adopted 3-2, which he moved); other OCII minutes on ex.sfocii.org are unreachable here

search_log.query: Rule applied to all three District 10 candidates in this package: a track-record item needs a government record documenting an outcome of the candidate's own official action (legislation, budget, program); self-reported results on campaign pages and questionnaires are not government records, and votes as one member of an appointed commission on minutes, reports or single project approvals are not recorded as performance outcomes
